text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The ruling Islamist Welfare Party spends billions of Turkish lira from a hardship fund in its hunt for votes.
- The Islamist-led government turns a blind eye to essential issues for Turkey -- such as high inflation, membership of the European Union and Cyprus -- because of internal politics.
- Tensions between the ruling Islamists and secularist army are exacerbated by the broadcasting on private television of two poems by an Islamist MP which target the military.
- The two wings of the coalition cannot agree on eight-year compulsory education.
- Universities enter the week with their agendas full of demonstrations.
- The president opposes government efforts to put pressure on the military.
- The State Planning Institute's March report says economic balances are on a knife-edge.
- A company in the western port city of Izmir gears up to sign a contract with Israel on selling 80 to 90 tonnes of lamb for $400,000 per month.
